properties.description: Construction of the Chelan Wet Weather Storage Tank located at 4034 West Marginal Way SW. There will be a new above-grade 4,995-sf one-story facility building (approx. 111-ft x 45-ft) with a concrete slab foundation on structural fill that will include: a 1,400-sf generator room (approx. 25-ft x 56-ft), a 1,258-sf electrical room (approx. 17-ft x 74-ft), a 48-sf restroom (approx. 6-ft x 8-ft), a 240-sf communication room (approx. 15-ft x 16-ft), and a 1,247-sf C2 room (approx. 29-ft x 43-ft) with a utility area, hydropneumatics tank, C2 booster pumps, tipping bucket valves, and air gap tank. A new above grade 2,250-sf architecturally screened odor control area (approx. 50-ft x 45-ft) with a concrete slab foundation on structural fill that will include: architectural screening (approx. 10-ft in height), dual bed scrubber, enclosed fan, filter, raised platform, and roof access. A new above-grade 4,200-sf one-story tipping bucket enclosure (approx. 300-ft x 13-ft) with a concrete slab foundation on structural fill. The new building footprint areas total 11,445-sf (facility building, screened odor control area, and tipping bucket enclosure). New at-grade impervious pavement areas and landscaping that include: an 11,514-sf fire apparatus road, a 3,857-sf maintenance access road, and 1,143-sf of parking with 6 stalls total (2 EV and 4 for maintenance). A new 7,078-sf stormwater bioretention cell providing water quality and infiltration for targeted surfaces and 1,066 linear feet of new fencing to include 2 new vehicular access gates. A new below-grade 37,500-sf, 7 MG storage tank (approx. 300-ft x 125-ft) with structural fill foundation material and associated channels and mechanical facilities that include: five flushing channels, a collection channel, and pump sump. There will be new access hatches (4 total) and a new 288-sf drain pump vault (approx. 12-ft x 24-ft). The new construction areas total is 68,950-sf with new and replaced impervious surfaces totaling 66,570-sf with total site excavation of 81,900-cy.

PROJECT GOALS 
A. Demolish existing warehouse structure, the CFS building, and above grade 
infrastructure in preparation for the redevelopment of the Terminal 5 Container 
Yard Expansion. 
B. Deliver 6 acres of pavement per requirements.  
C. Ensure all below grade vaults, lids, and Longfellow Creek pipe are rated for loading conditions per Civil Design Criteria.  
D. Provide 90-foot access between existing terminal and expanded area. 
E. Installation of new utilities to support the new facility per requirements.  
F. Installation of new fencing.  
G. Construction shall have minimal impacts to cargo operations and any impacts 
shall be coordinated with Port of Seattle Construction Management and 
terminal operator with at least 14 days advance notification.

properties.description:
*Application should be a shoreline EX, Proposal moved to 6968670-EX

Application in response to Shoreline Violations: 1054442-VI, 1055014-VI
Make demarcation on my property between the public Shore View Street End and my property adjacent to the South on the beach.  The SDOT will not fence or sign this street end, per Omar Akari.  Although he did say I could use temporary dune fencing.

Public used to use these 117 feet of beach (my 60', street end 20' and North adjacent 37' for partying wildly when both residences were inhabited by owners who had dementia for 5-10. Years.  The public still wants to trespass on my beach and tidelands, leaving behind dog waste, alcohol bottles, smoking paraphernalia, trash, condoms, etc. They also wish to launch small watercraft off and back onto my beach and tidelands, picnic, run in my sand yard after my dog and cat, yell at me when I very politely ask them to use the public area adjacent , or enjoy LIncoln Park just to the north 1/4 mile away.  People come to this tiny street end because  leave their dogs off leash, bc they see the private beach owners with their dogs.

I need some demarcation of my property.  I prefer as high a fence as you permit, to keep public from staring in my yard, yelling at me & my dog and cat.  Some public are violent.

***. I need the Shoreline Permit Exemption for Dune fencing, or driftwood fence perpendicular to the water on my private property within the allowable feet from the concrete bulkhead. It's a small, very low impact tiny project.

When the public gets aggressive and violent, is when I put up the bamboo higher fencing, to protect myself and my animals from them, and to keep my dry and wet sand sanitary.  It also protects the public's health and safety be containing them to their area, where they can see the trash and live with it, or pick it up.  

Technically, as I understand it this is a Shore View only Street End.  Public is not to access the water except during high tide, and not to infringe on the private dry and wet sand private property here.  I am okay with them walking straight down to the water's edge, and walking - keep moving along the shoreline.  They are not entitled to this, but as long as they comply and my property line is clearly marked, I can give this.

The City should be responsible for protecting both the public and the private citizens who pay big taxes to live here.

properties.description:
The area under our waterfront deck (9ft x12ft) was backfilled with construction debris, beach sand and clay chunks. The debris included several unsightly large chunks of concrete  leaning against the support for the deck. Additionally, there is an old drainage pipe that is failing. We want to clear the debris, improve and re-connect the drainage, and add a small  wood and post wall (3ft high x12 ft wide), to hide the foundation and drainage pipes and provide storage for our kayak and SUP. There are existing concrete stairs and a large concrete chunks which we want to mortar together to make a sitting area and walkway access for SUP storage. 

The face of the seawall has some cracks, but is otherwise sound. We would like to fill the voids with concrete patch to slow the degradation of the surface. 

On the east boundary of our property, along the driveway, we want to move the east fence line 4 feet out, to the property line. This will involve removing a 4'x20' paved strip which will then be maintained as permeable landscaping. Changes to the fence line does not impact the neighbors view.  

The purpose of the moving the fence line is to secure our property, enclose our dog, provide privacy and visibly establish our ownership. This is, in part, a response to 5 years of litigation by our neighbor who attempted to adversely possess that portion of our property which was outside the original fence line. She lost in court twice, at great expense to all concerned. Her home is built within 8 feet of our mutual north-south property line. A later remodel added stairs and landing 1 foot from the property line, affording us little privacy and fueling her desire for our land. Her home has been a rental property for 5 years and is about to go on the market. We do not want to go through this again with a new neighbor. 

Thank you.

properties.description:
The King County Wastewater Treatment Division (WTD) proposes to conduct maintenance repairs on the existing Denny Way combined sewer overflow (CSO) regulator. This WTD facility exists mostly on parcel number 7666202251, although the work area will extend onto the adjacent parcel 7666202250 (owned by Seattle Parks and Recreation) and Seattle right-of-way (ROW, owned by SDOT). There is no address associated with these parcels or ROW. The existing concrete pavilion overlays and protects the subterranean outfall gates of the CSO regulator and is surrounded by a protective layer of large diameter seawall rock (riprap) on the shoreline of Elliot Bay. Wave and tidal action against the riprap and pavilion have begun to erode the pavilion structure, putting the outfall gates at risk. The project therefore proposes to stabilize the plaza wall footing subgrade, repair damage in the seawall, and prevent further erosion of the shoreline around the Denny Way Regulator and Plaza. This project includes the removal of existing riprap to expose the plaza wall footings that have been undermined by tidal and wave action. The footing subgrade will be stabilized by pumping low strength concrete or flowable fill into the void spaces created by erosion of granular material from beneath the footings. Upon completion of stabilizing the plaza wall footings, the seawall will be repaired by replacing existing rock removed to repair the footings. Additional large diameter rock import will be placed to build up the shoreline revetment to protect the plaza walls and regulator transition structure.  Repair of the seawall will stabilize the shoreline, prevent further erosion around the Denny Way regulator, and restore the integrity of the surrounding plaza walls and concrete hardscape. The project will also increase the safety of staff working at the Regulator after dark and protect the Plaza's integrated artwork. 

The project construction will occur above the High Tide Line (HTL) that occurs at 10 feet NAVD88. All project work will be conducted in the dry. Temporary fencing will be erected in the surrounding upland areas to create a high-visibility barrier between the project site and the park-users. For site access a temporary construction access road and construction haul route will be established from the intersection of Broad Street and Alaskan Way along the Elliott Bay Trail. Environmentally critical areas (ECAs) and shoreline occur within or near the project area. No vegetation will be impacted by the project.

properties.description: Seattle Public Utilities is proposing to construct an underground storage tunnel to reduce the amount of sewage and stormwater (combined sewage) that discharges to the Lake Washington Ship Canal. A component of the project is the East Shaft and associated facilities.  The property currently serves as a parking lot and is secured by fencing on all sides; all structures/buildings were removed in 2015.  The East Shaft will serve as the retrieval shaft for the tunnel boring machine and will house a below-grade drop structure and odor control.  An above-grade 24' by 13'4" electrical building will be located on the eastern portion of the site.  Retaining walls will be constructed along the north and east property lines and at the southwest corner of the property (maximum height is approximately 5 feet at the NE corner of the property.  Following construction, landscaping will consist of:  street trees along Interlake Ave N, hydroseeding of the northern portion of the site for flexibility of repurposing, buffer planting along the perimeter of the driveway and SPU facilities for screening, and a bioretention swale along the fence line adjacent to Interlake Ave N

The property currently serves as a parking lot and is secured by fencing on all sides; all structures/buildings were removed in 2015.  The East Shaft will serve as the retrieval shaft for the tunnel boring machine and will house a below-grade drop structure and odor control.  An above-grade 24' by 13'4" electrical building will be located on the eastern portion of the site.  Retaining walls will be constructed along the north and east property lines and at the southwest corner of the property (maximum height is approximately 5 feet at the NE corner of the property.  Following construction, landscaping will consist of:  street trees along Interlake Ave N, hydroseeding of the northern portion of the site for flexibility of repurposing, buffer planting along the perimeter of the driveway and SPU facilities for screening, and a bioretention swale along the fence line adjacent to Interlake Ave N. 3500 INTERLAKE AVE N
